To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we derive an upper bound of both the power and the outage probabilities of the sensor in an RF-powered SWIPT system, and the upper bound becomes tight when the number of ambient RF transmitters is large.
the power outage probability is a decreasing function of the path-loss exponent, and the transmission outage probability is an increasing function of the path loss exponent.

the power and transmission outage performances of a wireless sensor in an ambient RF energy harvesting system can be improved by increasing the density of the ambient RF transmitters and the transmit power of the access point.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the performance of a RF-powered wireless sensor with the power-split SWIPT architecture in a network with ambient RF transceivers.
the performance of a SWIPT system with the ambient RF energy harvesting technique.

the performance analysis of a sensor with SWIPT capability in the downlink transmission, which is a fundamental building block in the design of future wireless networks with energy harvesting capability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our results provide useful insights into the performance of SWIPT systems in the context of ambient RF energy harvesting.
the performance of a RF-powered sensor with SWIPT in a DPP network is significantly better than that with SWIPT under the Poisson point network model.

the performance of the sensor is significantly improved by increasing the number of ambient RF transmitters, while the performance is degraded by increasing the path loss factor and the ambient noise power.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ambient RF transmitters can be modeled as a Ginibre a-DPP to achieve the desired performance of a sensor in an RF-powered SWIPT system.
we provide an accurate performance analysis of a sensor in a SWIPT network with ambient RF transceivers, and our work can be applied to a variety of RF energy harvesting networks.
the ambient RF energy harvesting technique can improve the energy harvesting rate of wireless devices and thus prolong the lifetime of the wireless sensor network.

the performance of the sensor is highly dependent on the distribution of the ambient RF transmitters.
